newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia looks at army in jobs assault - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia looks at army in jobs assault - paper.

text.p: The Australian government is considering voluntary training at army camps for young unemployed to help cut the stubbornly high unemployment rate, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Monday.

The plan is modelled on a New Zealand scheme, where unemployed people aged between 18 and 25 can choose a six-week training course focussing on motivational skills, physical exercise and discipline, the newspaper said.
Australian Employment Department officials had been pushing a similar plan, it said without citing any sources.
Prime Minister John Howard has already announced another voluntary scheme that would see young unemployed work in return for their unemployment benefits.
Vocational Education and Training Minister David Kemp is due to present a submission on that plan to senior ministers on Tuesday.
Australia's unemployment rate -- 8.6 percent in January -- has remain stuck around 8.5 percent for more than a year.
The government has forecast unemployment at 8.5 percent by the end of the 1996/97 fiscal year on June 30.
